cuotsq:295: On cheap GPUs without NVLink (e.g., RTX PRO 6000), PCIe bandwidth is only 1/14 of NVLink, and tensor parallelism all-reduce overhead jumps from 8–11% to 40–75%. The standard solution is to buy NVLink; Morphllm's solution is: (1) hide PCIe all-reduce latency via compute overlap; (2) share prefix caches across machines over TCP. The key is that even though TCP transport is an order of magnitude slower than RDMA, as long as the cache hit rate is high enough, fetching cache from a neighbor machine over TCP is faster than local recomputation—the savings from skipping prefill offset the slow transfer.
